items.description: Kick, snare, kick, snare: four sounds in one cycle.

items.pattern: bd sd bd sd bd sd bd sd

items.hint: Four steps. Rests on the first three, kick on the last.
Kick on beat 1 and beat 4, rests in between.
Two layers separated by a comma: kick on every beat, clap on 2 and 4.
The hat is on the "and" of each beat: a rest then a hat, four times.
Eight steps, three kicks. Write it out, or use the shortcut from this section.
Five kicks spread over eight steps. The shortcut is the easy way.

parts.label: s
parts.title: The sound function
parts.detail: Short for "sound". It plays the sounds named inside its parentheses.

parts.title: Parentheses
parts.detail: Hand the function something to work with. Every function has them, and they always come in pairs.

parts.title: Quotes
parts.detail: Everything between the quotes is mini-notation: the rhythm language.

parts.label: bd*4
parts.title: Layer 1 (mini-notation)
parts.detail: Kick drum, four times per cycle: every beat.

parts.title: Layer separator (mini-notation)
parts.detail: Starts another layer that plays at the same time.

parts.label: ~ cp ~ cp
parts.title: Layer 2 (mini-notation)
parts.detail: Rest, clap, rest, clap: clap on beats 2 and 4.

parts.title: Closing parenthesis
parts.detail: The s(…) function is complete. A missing one of these is the most common error.

parts.label: .bank
parts.title: A chained function
parts.detail: The dot says "and then". It takes what came before and changes it. This one picks the drum machine.

parts.label: "RolandTR909"
parts.title: The machine name
parts.detail: A name, so it goes in quotes.

parts.label: .gain
parts.title: Another chained function
parts.detail: Volume. 1 is normal, 0.5 is about half.

parts.title: A plain number
parts.detail: A single number needs no quotes.

quiz.question: Tap the part that decides when the clap plays.
quiz.explanation: ~ cp ~ cp is the rhythm for the clap, inside the quotes.

quiz.question: Tap the part that chooses the drum machine.
quiz.explanation: .bank("RolandTR909") picks the machine. It sits outside the rhythm quotes.

quiz.question: Tap a function.
quiz.explanation: Functions are the names before parentheses: s, .bank and .gain.

quiz.question: Tap the character you'd most likely forget, and break the line.
quiz.explanation: The closing ) of s(…). It's easy to lose because it sits right after the closing quote.

quiz.question: Tap the part that makes the clap and kick play at the same time.
quiz.explanation: The comma inside the quotes stacks layers on top of each other.

items.hint: Count the parentheses. How many open, how many close?
items.explanation: Every ( needs a ). The (1:15) in the message means line 1, character 15: the very end of the line. Strudel got there still waiting for a ), so the problem is at, or just before, that spot.

items.hint: Look at the drum machine name.
items.explanation: Names need quotes too: .bank("RolandTR909"). Without them, Strudel looks for something in the code called RolandTR909 and finds nothing, so it says "not defined".

items.hint: How does one function connect to the next?
items.explanation: Chained functions start with a dot. The dot means "and then do this to it".

item.hint: Three layers: four-on-the-floor kick, clap on 2 and 4, open hat on the off-beats.
Look at the very first character.
item.explanation: Code is case-sensitive. s is the sound function; S is nothing.

item.description: Three kicks spread over eight steps (the tresillo), plus eighth-note hi-hats.

item.hint: Four steps. Step 3 is split, with the kick on its second half.

item.explanation: Without quotes, Strudel tries to read the rhythm as code. It gets as far as bd*4, (which happens to look like math) and stops at ~, character 13, because ~ means nothing in code. The quotes tell Strudel "this is a rhythm, not code".
